questions.stem: Particles can move by diffusion, osmosis or active transport. Select the example of active transport.

options.A: The smell of deodorant or perfume
options.B: Water being absorbed into plant roots
options.C: Concentrated fruit juice mixing with water in a glass
options.D: Absorption of nitrate molecules by plants

questions.explanation: The absorption of nitrate molecules by plants is an example of active transport. This is the net (overall) movement of particles from an area of lower concentration to a higher one and requires energy. The smell of deodorant or perfume is an example of diffusion. This is the net (overall) movement of molecules from an area of higher to lower concentration. It can happen in liquids and gases only. A second example of diffusion is concentrated fruit juice being diluted by water. Water being absorbed into plant roots is an example of osmosis. questions.stem: Arteries, veins and capillaries are all blood vessels. These carry oxygen and other vital substances around the body. Identity the correct adaptation of veins.

options.A: Have thick, elastic walls to withstand high pressure
options.C: One-way valves stop backflow of blood
options.D: Have thin walls to allow substances to move in/out of them easily

questions.explanation: Veins have one-way valves that stop the backflow of blood. These are needed because blood returns to the heart in veins and so is under lower pressure than in arteries or capillaries. Arteries take blood away from the heart immediately after each heartbeat. Therefore the blood is under high pressure and so arteries require thick, elastic walls. This means that they also therefore have a narrow lumen (the gap in the middle of blood vessels in which blood flows). Arteries take blood to the tissues and organs of the body from where it passes into capillaries within these structures. Capillaries h

questions.stem: Black spot is a communicable disease which infects roses. Identify the type of pathogen which causes this disease.
questions.explanation: Rose black spot is caused by a fungus which makes black and purple spots on leaves. These reduce photosynthesis in the infected plant and so slows growth. A common example of a virus that infects plants is the Tobacco Mosaic Virus. As well as infecting tobacco plants, it also infects closely related species like tomatoes and peppers. It changes the colour of leaves to yellow or white which reduces photosynthesis in the infected plant and so slows growth. There are no specific bacterial infections of plants that you need to learn about. Insects such as aphids can infest many plants. They suck t

questions.stem: Energy is released from glucose in respiration. Which of these processes does not require energy from respiration?
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the net (overall) movement of molecules from an area of higher concentration to a lower one. This process does not require energy. So the diffusion of oxygen from the alveoli in the lungs to the blood happens without energy from respiration. Mitosis is a type of cell division which makes two genetically identical daughter cells for growth and repair. This requires energy from respiration. Homeostasis is the maintenance of your body's internal environment. It includes keeping temperature, blood glucose level and water content in the blood constant. These processes all require energ

questions.stem: The menstrual cycle is controlled by hormones made in glands. It is represented in the image above. Select the correct labels for the three coloured lines representing hormone concentration during the cycle.

options.A: A - Oestrogen B - FSH C - LH
options.B: A - LH B - FSH C - Oestrogen
options.C: A - Oestrogen B - Progesterone C - FSH
options.D: A - Glucagon B - Insulin C - Progesterone

questions.explanation: The levels of oestrogen increase from the beginning of the cycle to peak around day 12. FSH peaks several days afterwards which causes the maturation of an egg in an ovary. This is quickly flowed by a noticeable increase in LH which causes ovulation. So Label A is oestrogen, label B is FSH and label C is LH. Progesterone is a hormone of the menstrual cycle but not shown in this diagram. Levels of progesterone drop off at the end of the cycle to trigger a period (menstruation) or remain high if a woman is pregnant. Glucagon and insulin are hormones but regulate blood sugar not the menstrual cyc

questions.stem: Variation is described as differences between individuals of the same species. It can be caused by genetic factors and/or environmental factors. Select the example of variation caused by both genetic and environmental factors.
questions.explanation: Height is an example of variation that is caused by both genetic and environmental factors. Tall parents often pass genes for being tall to their children, meaning they have the potential to grow to be like their parents. However, if their diet is poor they may not grow to be this tall. This would be their environment (diet) having an effect. There are four different blood groups - A, B, AB and O. Your blood group is determined by the genes in the sperm and egg you grew from. So it is an example of genetic variation. Eye colour is the same, so another example of genetic variation. A person's s

Algal blooms with depleted oxygen: algae quickly grow to cover the surface of the water stopping light reaching other plants which die B. questions.stem: A student investigates the rate of photosynthesis of an aquatic plant at different light intensities. They recorded the number of bubbles of oxygen produced in a minute at different light intensities (1/d2). Their results are shown in the graph above. Determine the numbers of bubbles they might have expected when 1/d2 is 0.008.
questions.explanation: To determine the numbers of bubbles they might have expected when 1/d2 is 0.008, you would draw a vertical line upwards from this reading on the x axis until it hits the green line of best fit on the graph. Then you would turn to the left and draw a horizontal line towards the y axis. The value on the y axis that this line hits is the correct answer to this question. It is 95, not 120, 58 nor 0

questions.stem: Specialised plant and animal cells have different cellular components. Select the statement which is correct from the list below.

options.A: Animal cells have a cell wall and plant cells do not
options.B: Only plant cells have permanent vacuoles
options.D: Plant cells have plasmids and animal cells do not

questions.explanation: Only plant cells have permanent vacuoles and animal cells do not. They help plant cells retain the correct volume of water. Some animal cells have temporary vacuoles but these are often much smaller than those in plant cells. It is plant cells that have cell walls and not animal cells. Both have membranes. Not all plant cells have chloroplasts. These often turn the cells of plants a green colour. Plant root cells are usually white because they do not have chloroplasts. They do not need them because they do not do photosynthesis under the ground. Only bacterial cells have plasmids. These are sm

questions.stem: A student completed an experiment involving osmosis of water in potatoes placed into different salt concentrations. The first piece of potato had a mass of 1.4 g before the experiment and 1.3 g after being placed into the solution. What percentage change in mass is this? Give your answer to one decimal place
questions.explanation: Percentage change is calculated as follows: ((1.4 - 1.3) ÷ 1.4) × 100 = -7 %

questions.stem: Plants and animals are eukaryotes. Bacteria are prokaryotes. Select the cellular component which is only found in prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: Plasmids are small, circular sections of DNA that are found in the cytoplasm of prokaryotes (bacteria) only. They can move between bacterial cells and are a source of variation. Mitochondria are the site of respiration in eukaryotic cells. This is where energy is released from glucose so the cell can fulfil its function. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in eukaryotic cells. So they are the place in these cells where proteins are made. The genetic information (DNA) is found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. Bacteria do not have nuclei in their cells.

questions.stem: Coronary disease is a major cause of death in the UK and worldwide. Identify the medical treatment for cardiovascular disease.
questions.explanation: Stents are a medical treatment for coronary heart disease. They are small sections of mesh which are inflated within a coronary artery using a small balloon. They squash any fatty blockage to the sides of the artery and allow blood flow to return to normal. Chemotherapy is used to treat cancerous tumours. Antibiotics are used to treat bacterial infections. (It is a common mistake to think they treat viral infections.) Inhalers are used to treat problems with the gas exchange system like asthma.

questions.stem: Antibiotics are life-saving medicines. Some microorganisms are becoming resistant to specific antibiotics. Select the statement about antibiotic resistance which is true.

options.B: It decreases when we use more antibiotics
options.C: It is less common in hospitals
options.D: It means we can use antibiotics to treat virus infections

questions.explanation: Antibiotic resistance is evidence for evolution. The first instances of bacteria evolving to become resistant to our first antibiotic (Penicillin) occurred only a few years after the drug's widespread use. Antibiotic resistance increases when we use these medicines more frequently. Antibiotic resistance is more common in hospitals which is why hospitals practice high levels of hygiene including hand washing. Antibiotics can only be used to treat bacterial infections because they do not kill viruses.

questions.stem: The rate of photosynthesis can be slowed by limiting factors including temperature. Which of these graphs shows the effects of temperature upon the rate of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Graph A is the correct shape to show the effects of temperature on photosynthesis. As the temperature increases, the rate increases until an optimum temperature is reached. Beyond this, enzymes are denatured and so the rate of photosynthesis slows and stops quite rapidly. Graph B shows the effects of increasing concentration of carbon dioxide upon photosynthesis. The maximum rate occurs when the line becomes horizontal and any further increase in carbon dioxide has no effect. The rate is limited by another factor. Graph C shows the effects of increasing concentration of carbon dioxide upon pho

questions.stem: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant internal environment. An example is maintaining blood sugar concentrations. Identify the statement that is correct when blood sugar is high.

options.A: Insulin is stopped from being released into the blood and so glycogen is not formed
options.B: Glucagon is released into the blood and glycogen is formed
options.C: Insulin is released into the blood and glycogen is formed
options.D: Glycogen is released into the blood and glucose is formed

questions.explanation: Blood sugar is also called glucose. When levels of glucose are high the pancreas releases the hormone insulin which converts glucose to glycogen. This reduces blood sugar levels back to normal.

questions.stem: The relationships between the evolution of organisms can be shown in an evolutionary tree. Which two organisms are the closest evolved to E?
questions.explanation: The oldest part of the tree is at the top. The split between A and B and all others came first because this is the first branch. The splits between A and B, C and D and F and G are the most recent because they are lowest on the tree. E split from F and G, which then split themselves. So E is closest to F and G. It is important to remember which is the oldest and newest part of the tree to help here.

questions.stem: Climate change is occurring because of the enhanced greenhouse effect. Select the example that is a consequence of climate change.
questions.explanation: Climate change is causing some species to migrate away from the hotter areas around the equator towards the poles. Climate change is causing the average temperature of tropical seas to increase, resulting in the bleaching of coral. It isn't making them colder. The effects of climate change on weather are unpredictable. Some areas are likely to have less rain, whilst other areas are likely to have more. Climate change is resulting in the melting of polar ice caps which is causing sea levels to rise, not the ice caps themselves to rise.

questions.stem: Many practical activities involving microorganisms require the use of aseptic technique. Which of these is an example of this technique?
questions.explanation: Aseptic technique is a range of procedures which prevent the contamination of cultures growing in laboratories by unwanted microorganisms. Flaming equipment means passing it through a flame (often from a Bunsen burner) to sterilise it. This is therefore an example of aseptic technique. Cultures of microorganisms are often grown on agar plates, but this in itself is not an example of aseptic technique. Chromatography is a way of separating inks using a solvent. This is not an example of aseptic technique. Fractional distillation is a way of separating the different substances within crude oil.

questions.stem: The effectiveness of antibiotics can be determined by placing them on paper disks which are in turn placed upon microorganisms growing on an agar plate. Identify why a paper disk with only water and no antibiotic was placed in position 4.

options.A: Because they didn't have enough other antibiotics
options.B: To repeat one antibiotic from a previous investigation
options.C: To prove that it was the antibiotic not the paper disk
options.D: To calculate the area of clearing

questions.explanation: The paper disk with water on it acted as a control in this experiment. It proved that that the areas of clearing in the other samples were due to the antibiotic, not the paper disk. Scientists often repeat experiments but position 4 was not a repeat this time. Scientists calculate the area of clearing using the equation 𝜋r2

questions.stem: The width of a human hair is 100 μm andthe diameter of a virus is 100 nm. What is the difference in order of magnitude between the widths of these two structures?
questions.explanation: There are 1000 nanometres (nm) in a micrometre (μm). So there are 100000 nm in 100 μm. 100 is 1 × 102 and 100000 is 1 × 105 The difference between these is an order of magnitude of 3

questions.stem: Select which one of these is only found in a plant cell.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall outside the cell membrane, which strengthens the cell, helping to support the plant. Both animal and plant cells have a nucleus, a cell membrane and cytoplasm.

questions.stem: Select which one of the following is not a type of blood vessel.
questions.explanation: Alveoli are the air sacs inside the lungs. They enable gas exchange between the air in the lungs and the bloodstream. They are not blood vessels.

questions.stem: Each element in the periodic table has an atomic number. Select which one of the following statements describes the atomic number.

options.A: The number of protons in the atom
options.B: The number of neutrons in the atom
options.C: The number of protons and the number of neutrons in the atom
options.D: The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in the atom

questions.explanation: The atomic number shows the number of protons in the nucleus of one atom of the element. The mass number shows the number of protons plus the number of neutrons present in the nucleus.

questions.stem: State which one of the following compounds is an example of ionic bonding.
questions.explanation: Ionic bonding takes places when a metal reacts with a non-metal. The only one of the options that this applies to is sodium chloride. Sodium is a metal, and chlorine is a non-metal.

questions.stem: This is a series circuit. Select which one of the following statements is true about this type of circuit.

options.A: The current divides in the circuit and then recombines
options.B: There is the same current through each component
options.C: The potential difference supplied by the cell is equal to the potential difference across each component
options.D: The total resistance of the two components is the same as the resistance of each component.

questions.explanation: In a series circuit there is only one path for the current to take so it cannot divide. The same amount of current flows through all parts of the circuit. The potential difference supplied has to be shared between the components. The resistances of the individual components are added together to calculate the total resistance of the circuit.

questions.stem: Hydrochloric acid will react with sodium hydroxide to produce water and a salt. What is the name of the salt formed?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is formed. When an acid reacts with a base, the name of the salt produced has two parts. The first part of the name comes from the metal part of the base - in this case sodium, from sodium hydroxide. The second part of the name comes from the acid used: Hydrochloric acid produces a chloride salt. Other acids form different salts: Sulfuric acid produces sulfate salts Nitric acid produces nitrate salts

questions.stem: The density of a material can be calculated from its mass and its volume. Use the formula above to calculate the density of a block of concrete with a volume of 20 cm3 and a mass of 48 g.
questions.explanation: Density is calculated by dividing the mass by the volume so the 48 g needs to be divided by the 20 cm3 Density = mass ÷ volumeDensity = 48 ÷ 20Density = 2.4 g/cm3

questions.stem: A train accelerates from a speed of 10 m/s up to 30 m/s. It takes 40 s to reach this speed. Use the formula above to calculate its acceleration.
questions.explanation: Change in velocity = 30 - 10 = 20 m/s Acceleration = 20 ÷ 40 = 0.5 m/s2

questions.stem: These four metals all appear in the reactivity series. Which of these shows them in the correct order, from most reactive to least reactive?
questions.explanation: The correct order is potassium, lithium, zinc, copper. • Potassium is the most reactive and will react with air and (vigorously) with water. • Lithium's reaction with water is less vigorous. • Zinc does not react with water, but reacts slowly with a dilute acid • Copper does not react with a dilute acid.

questions.stem: This diagram shows a cross-sectional view of a green leaf. Select which type of tissue is highlighted by the rectangle.
questions.explanation: The correct name for this layer of cells is the spongy mesophyll. This is where gas exchange takes place within the leaf. Photosynthesis mostly takes place in the palisade mesophyll layer, as this is where the cells contain the most chloroplasts.

questions.stem: A student looks at part of a plant through a microscope. The object appears to be 4 mm wide when viewed through the microscope but is actually 0.04mm wide. What is the magnification?
questions.explanation: Magnification = image size ÷ object size Magnification = 4 ÷ 0.04 Magnification = x100

questions.stem: Select which one of the following is a product of photosynthesis.

Some characteristics in living things are controlled by a single gene. These genes have different forms, or alleles. The alleles can be dominant or recessive. Select which one of the following statements is true.

options.A: The dominant allele is never expressed, even if present
options.B: The recessive allele is always expressed, if present
options.C: The recessive allele is only expressed if two recessive alleles are inherited
options.D: The dominant allele is only expressed if two dominant alleles are inherited

questions.explanation: One allele is inherited from each parent. If one or both are dominant alleles, this trait will be expressed. If both are recessive then it will be this characteristic which will be expressed.

questions.stem: Look at this food web. A disease breaks out in the local rabbit population and significantly reduces their numbers in the ecosystem. Select which one of the following is more likely to be observed over the next few weeks.
questions.explanation: If there are fewer rabbits, the plants will be eaten less and so their population will increase. The lower rabbit population will mean less food for predators so the falcon and fox populations are likely to decrease. Although the mice may have more to eat, they may be preyed upon more if there are fewer rabbits to catch, so their population may increase, decrease or stay the same.

questions.stem: Group 1 of the Periodic Table includes elements such as sodium and potassium. Read the four statements and select the one that is true.

options.A: Group 1 elements become more reactive going down the group
options.B: Group 1 elements all have seven electrons in their outermost shell
options.C: Group 1 elements do not react with water

questions.explanation: Group 1 elements become more reactive as you go down the group in the Periodic Table. These elements are all metals, and have a single electron in their outer shell. They all react with water.

questions.stem: Read the four statements about the arrangement of particles in a solid, liquid and gas. Select the statement that is true.

options.A: Solids have a fixed shape and volume because the particles are held in a rigid pattern
options.B: The container determines the shape and volume of a liquid, as the particles are free to move
options.C: Solids are compressible, as there are gaps between the particles.
options.D: The particles in a gas vibrate about a fixed point, so a gas has a fixed volume

questions.explanation: A solid has a fixed shape due to the strong forces between particles. They have no gaps between particles so they are incompressible; therefore, they have a fixed volume. Liquids are able to flow because their particles are able to move, so they can take any shape. However, intermolecular forces prevent particles moving freely, so they cannot change their volume. The particles in a gas are free to move, so they can take any shape or any volume.

questions.stem: Hydrochloric acid reacts with magnesium. State the gas formed in the reaction.
Select the correct description of an exothermic reaction.

options.A: A reaction in which energy is absorbed from the surroundings
options.B: A reaction in which large amounts of energy are transferred
options.C: A reaction in which energy is transferred to the surroundings
options.D: A reaction in which gases are released into the atmosphere

questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction is one in which energy is transferred from the reactants to the surroundings.

questions.stem: A light bulb transfers 600 J of energy every minute.Calculate the power rating of the bulb in watts.
questions.explanation: Power is a measurement of the rate at which energy is transferred. One watt of power is equivalent to one joule of energy being transferred every second. Remember that time must be converted into seconds before using in the equation: Time = 1 minute = 60s Power = energy ÷ timePower = 600 ÷ 60Power = 10 W

questions.stem: A solenoid is a type of electromagnet, made by wrapping a wire into a coil and passing a current through it. The coil will then produce a magnetic field. Select which one of these changes will cause an increase in the strength of the magnetic field.

options.A: Reducing the number of turns in the coil of wire
options.B: Decreasing the current in the coil
options.C: Reversing the direction in which current flows through the coil
options.D: Placing an iron core in the centre of the coil

questions.explanation: Adding an iron core increases the strength of an electromagnet. Decreasing the current, or the number of turns, reduces the electromagnet's strength. Reversing the current flow will reverse the direction of the magnetic field but won't affect its strength.

questions.stem: Which option shows the correct description of the subatomic particles in a potassium atom?

options.A: 19 positive protons, 19 negative electrons, 39 neutral neutrons
options.B: 19 negative protons, 39 positive electrons, 10 neutral neutrons
options.C: 19 positive protons, 19 negative electrons, 20 neutral neutrons
options.D: 19 neutral protons, 19 positive neutrons, 20 negative electrons

questions.explanation: Protons are positive, electrons are negative and neutrons are neutral (no charge). The atomic number tells you how many protons are in the nucleus of the atom - in this case 19. The positive protons are balanced by an equal number of negative electrons because the atom has no overall charge. Therefore, there are also 19 electrons in potassium. The number of neutrons is calculated by subtracting the number of protons from the mass number: 39 - 19 = 20 neutrons. An answer suggesting that each K atom has 39 neutrons is wrong because 39 is the mass number of this atom. The mass number is the numbe

questions.stem: Which statement describes and explains a property of the substance shown in the diagram?

options.A: This ionic substance will conduct electricity when dissolved in water because the ions will be able to move to carry a charge/current
options.B: This giant covalent substance has a very high melting point because there are many strong covalent bonds between the atoms
options.C: This covalent substance is made from small molecules so it will have a very low boiling point due to the weak forces between the molecules
options.D: This metal will be a good conductor of electricity because there are delocalised electrons which can move through the structure

questions.explanation: The diagram shows a giant ionic lattice because the positive and negative ions are shown. This means that it cannot be a covalent substance or a metal (metals are made only from positive ions, surrounded by delocalised electrons, with no negative ions present in the structure.) Ionic substances conduct electricity if or when they dissolve because the ions are free to move to carry a charge or current.

questions.stem: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium hydroxide. The relative atomic mass (Ar) of calcium is 40The relative atomic mass (Ar) of hydrogen is 1The relative atomic mass (Ar) of oxygen is 16
questions.explanation: When working out relative formula mass values for compounds with brackets, calculate the bit inside the brackets first, just like in maths. So the OH is equal to 17. The subscripted number 2 after the brackets means that we have to double the part inside the brackets, so (OH)2 is equal to 34. Then finally add on the part outside the brackets (40 for the Ca atom).

questions.stem: A student was asked to make pure dry crystals of magnesium nitrate, which is a soluble salt. Here is the method they used.1. Measure 30 cm3 of dilute nitric acid into a beaker.

options.A: The student used the wrong acid
options.B: The student should have used magnesium metal instead of magnesium oxide
options.C: The student should have filtered the mixture after step 2
options.D: The student should have heated the mixture until all the water had evaporated

questions.explanation: Filtering the mixture after step 2 would have removed the unreacted solid magnesium oxide. This would have meant that the liquid in the evaporating basin would have contained only magnesium nitrate dissolved in water, so the crystals at the end would have been pure, not contaminated with magnesium oxide. Nitric acid is the correct acid to use to make magnesium nitrate. Magnesium metal would have produced magnesium nitrate salt, but the reaction might have been too dangerous, so it is safer to use a metal oxide. Heating the mixture until all the water has evaporated would have resulted in small

questions.stem: Using the graph, what is the average rate of reaction during the first 15 seconds of the reaction?
questions.explanation: To calculate the average rate of reaction, you need to divide the volume of gas produced by the time taken to produce the gas. Find the value of 15 seconds on the x axis and draw a line vertically upwards until you hit the curve of the graph. Then follow a horizontal line to the left until you hit the y axis, to find the volume of gas. Divide the volume of gas (120) by the time (15) to find the average rate of reaction. 120 ÷ 15 = 8 cm3/s

questions.stem: Name the organic molecule in the diagram. The black spheres are carbon atoms and the white spheres are hydrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: The molecule in the diagram has single covalent bonds between all of its carbon atoms, so it is an alkane, meaning that its name ends with -ane. Alkanes have the general formula shown above and this molecule has three C atoms and eight H atoms, which fits with the general formula for alkanes. You need to know the names of the first four alkanes: methane, ethane, propane, butane. Use a mnemonic like 'monkeys eat peanut butter' to help you remember their names.

questions.stem: What is the Rf value of the red pigment shown on this chromatogram above?
questions.explanation: The Rf value is calculated by dividing the distance moved by the substance by the distance moved by the solvent, so 1.5 ÷ 6 = 0.25 Remember: Rf values will always be decimals and they will always be less than 1.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most accurate description of the composition of the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The early atmosphere probably contained high levels of carbon dioxide and ammonia, but scientists believe that for 200 million years the atmosphere has been approximately 80% nitrogen and 20% oxygen. Small amounts of other gases are also present, mainly argon. There is also a tiny amount of carbon dioxide - around 0.04%

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common stage in making potable water in the UK?
questions.explanation: Drinking water in the UK is usually obtained by the following steps 1.Selecting a suitable source of fresh water, such as a river or lake 2.Filtering the water 3.Sterilising with chlorine, ozone or UV light Aerobic and anaerobic digestion are involved in processing waste water (sewage). Desalination is used to remove salt from sea water to make it safe to drink (potable) but this technique is not widely used in the UK because there are lots of sources of fresh water and desalination is an expensive process which requires a lot of energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best explains why catalysts speed up the rate of a chemical reaction?

options.A: They provide the reactant particles with more energy so that successful collisions are more frequent
options.B: They have an active site which matches the shape of the substrate molecule, as explained by the 'lock and key' mechanism
options.C: Catalysts are specific to certain chemical reactions and speed them up without being used up or chemically changed
options.D: They provide an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy

questions.explanation: As shown by the energy profile diagram, adding a catalyst to a chemical reaction provides the reactant molecules with an alternative reaction pathway which has a lower activation energy. This means that more of the reactant molecules can react at any one instant. Catalysts do not provide the reactants with additional energy. Enzymes are proteins which acts as catalysts inside living organisms, but not all catalysts are enzymes and therefore not all catalysts work using the 'lock and key' model. Whilst catalysts can be described as chemicals which speed up a reaction without being used up or ch
